# spax: spatial accessibility and allocation modeling

`spax` supports two user workflows: public floating catchment area (FCA)
methods for accessibility surfaces, and an experimental static
conditional-logit model (CLM) workflow for fitting allocation to
observations, inspecting results, and evaluating supply scenarios. Both
use explicit demand, facility supply and travel inputs. Their
normalization and output meanings remain model-specific.

Existing
[`spax_2sfca()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/spax_2sfca.md),
[`spax_e2sfca()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/spax_e2sfca.md),
[`spax_m2sfca()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/spax_m2sfca.md)
and
[`compute_access()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/compute_access.md)
workflows remain supported, and the experimental
[`spax_3sfca()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/spax_3sfca.md)
and
[`spax_huff2sfca()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/spax_huff2sfca.md)
add selection-weighted variants. The allocation functions are an
additional route; they do not replace the FCA functions. Internal
feedback-model machinery is private and is not part of the experimental
CLM interface.

## Install

Use R 4.4.0 or newer. This is the supported dependency and testing floor
for spax 0.3.1. Existing public FCA calling semantics are unchanged.

Install version 0.3.1 by its release tag rather than from the
repository’s default branch:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("Songyosr/spax@v0.3.1")
```

The allocation interface is experimental and may change in later
versions. For reproducible work, record the package version and retain
the input IDs, units, observation declaration and saved results.
Development continues on the `develop` branch
(`pak::pak("Songyosr/spax@develop")`).

Each release is archived on Zenodo; <doi:10.5281/zenodo.23438611> refers
to all versions (version 0.3.0 is <doi:10.5281/zenodo.23438612>). Cite
the version you used with `citation("spax")`.

Package and function help are available from an installed package.
Installations that include built articles also provide the guides, which
follow one reader journey: Get started, the example data and data
preparation, the FCA guides, then the allocation model (model choice,
the workflow and bootstrap intervals):

``` r

# Package overview, and notes on reusing saved results
help(package = "spax")
help("spax-package", package = "spax")
help("allocation-compatibility", package = "spax")

# The guides
browseVignettes("spax")
# When the installation includes built vignettes:
vignette("spax", package = "spax")  # Get started
vignette("cornwall-data", package = "spax")
vignette("model-choice", package = "spax")
vignette("allocation-workflow", package = "spax")
vignette("facility-bootstrap", package = "spax")
```

## Quick start: GP practices in Cornwall

spax ships open example data for the 55 general practices of Cornwall
and the Isles of Scilly: practice locations and GP full-time equivalents
(FTE, excluding GPs in training) in `cornwall_gp`, small areas with
registered residents in `cornwall_lsoa`, small area × practice
registrations in `cornwall_flows` and travel minutes in
`cornwall_travel`, plus a WorldPop 2020 population grid and one
travel-time layer per practice. The Isles of Scilly have no road link to
the mainland, so this example models mainland Cornwall only: it drops
the islands’ practice and small area, and crops the islands from the
grids.
[`vignette("cornwall-data", package = "spax")`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/articles/cornwall-data.md)
describes each object, its sources and its licences.

### An FCA accessibility map

FCA entry points take a demand raster and one aligned travel layer per
facility, with layer names matching facility IDs.

``` r

library(spax)
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Mainland practices, as a plain table
mainland_gp <- cornwall_gp |>
  filter(!scilly) |>
  st_drop_geometry()

# Residents per grid cell, and travel minutes with one layer per practice;
# crop both to the mainland (west edge at 6 degrees W)
pop <- read_spax_example("cornwall_pop.tif")
travel_grid <- read_spax_example("cornwall_gp_travel.tif")
mainland <- ext(-6, xmax(pop), ymin(pop), ymax(pop))
pop <- crop(pop, mainland)
travel_grid <- crop(travel_grid[[mainland_gp$practice]], mainland)

fca <- spax_e2sfca(
  demand = pop,
  supply = mainland_gp,
  distance = travel_grid,
  decay_params = list(method = "gaussian", sigma = 10),
  id_col = "practice",  # matches supply rows to travel layers
  supply_cols = "gp_fte_extg"
)

plot(
  1000 * fca$accessibility,
  axes = FALSE,
  col = hcl.colors(50, "viridis"),
  main = "E2SFCA index, GP FTE per 1,000 residents"
)
```

![Raster map of the E2SFCA index for mainland Cornwall in GP FTE per
1,000 residents; values are highest in the west of the county and lowest
on Bodmin Moor and at the tips of the western
peninsulas.](reference/figures/README-fca-1.png)

This is an enhanced two-step FCA index: supply per distance-weighted
population, in GP FTE per 1,000 residents. The 10-minute Gaussian scale
is a choice for this example, not an estimate. The index is a
supply-per-demand score, not a probability that anyone uses a practice.
See
[`?spax_e2sfca`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/spax_e2sfca.md)
for decay and normalization options, and `summary(fca)` or `plot(fca)`
to inspect the result.

### A static CLM fitted to registrations

The CLM route takes numeric vectors and an origin-by-facility travel
matrix, and fits where people choose to go. Here demand is the residents
of each small area registered with any GP practice in England, supply is
GP FTE, and the target is the observed small area × practice
registrations. The model includes an outside option, which here stands
for registration with a practice outside mainland Cornwall (for example
in Devon or on the Isles of Scilly); it is not unmet need.

``` r

mainland_lsoa <- cornwall_lsoa |>
  filter(!scilly) |>
  st_drop_geometry()

# Travel minutes (small areas x practices), demand and supply, named by ID
travel <- cornwall_travel[mainland_lsoa$lsoa, mainland_gp$practice]
demand <- setNames(mainland_lsoa$registered, mainland_lsoa$lsoa)
supply <- setNames(mainland_gp$gp_fte_extg, mainland_gp$practice)

# Observed registrations as a small area x practice matrix (zero if none)
observed <- matrix(
  0,
  nrow = nrow(travel),
  ncol = ncol(travel),
  dimnames = dimnames(travel)
)
keep <- cornwall_flows$lsoa %in% rownames(travel) &
  cornwall_flows$practice %in% colnames(travel)
observed[cbind(cornwall_flows$lsoa[keep], cornwall_flows$practice[keep])] <-
  cornwall_flows$patients[keep]
```

``` r

# Check and align the inputs once; unit labels are recorded, not converted
inputs <- prepare_allocation(
  demand = demand,
  supply = supply,
  distance = travel,
  metadata = list(
    demand_units = "registered residents",
    demand_period = "July 2026",
    supply_units = "GP FTE excluding GPs in training",
    supply_period = "June 2026",
    travel_units = "minutes"
  )
)

# Gaussian travel decay with a fitted outside weight v0
model <- clm_allocation(inputs, family = "gaussian", fit_v0 = TRUE)

# Fit the flows from three explicit starts with a Poisson loss
starts <- rbind(
  near = c(sigma = 3, v0 = 0.05),
  middle = c(sigma = 6, v0 = 0.01),
  far = c(sigma = 12, v0 = 0.002)
)
fit <- fit_allocation(
  model = model,
  observed = observed,
  starts = starts,
  lower = c(sigma = 0.5, v0 = 1e-6),
  upper = c(sigma = 60, v0 = 10),
  output = "flow",
  loss = "poisson",
  gradient = TRUE,
  control = list(maxit = 300, factr = 10, pgtol = 1e-8)
)
coef(fit)
```

``` R
     sigma         v0 
4.59099724 0.02733454 
```

``` r

# Per cent registered outside mainland Cornwall: observed and modelled
outside <- c(
  observed = 1 - sum(observed) / sum(demand),
  modelled = 1 - sum(fitted(fit)) / sum(demand)
)
round(100 * outside, 2)
```

``` R
observed modelled 
    0.91     0.54 
```

``` r

# Practice totals: modelled against observed
cor(colSums(fitted(fit)), colSums(observed))
```

``` R
[1] 0.9326925
```

The fitted Gaussian scale is about 4.6 minutes: registration is very
local. The printed shares are percentages of registered residents.
Practice totals of the fitted flows correlate at 0.93 with the observed
ones. One constant outside weight understates registration outside
mainland Cornwall, which is concentrated in a few areas near the Devon
border. Poisson fitting is chosen explicitly (the fitting default is
weighted SSE); inspect `summary(fit)` for all starts, failures and
boundaries.

[`predict_allocation()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/predict_allocation.md)
returns choice probabilities for requested areas. For the practice with
the largest list, St Austell Health Group, the modelled probability can
be set beside the observed share of each area’s registered residents:

``` r

# Choice probabilities for every small area
prediction <- predict_allocation(
  source = fit,
  distance = travel,
  demand = demand,
  outputs = "allocation"
)

# Observed share and modelled probability for one practice, in one table
st_austell <- "Y04957"  # St Austell Health Group
shares <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(
    lsoa = rownames(travel),
    source = "Observed share",
    value = observed[, st_austell] / demand
  ),
  data.frame(
    lsoa = rownames(travel),
    source = "Modelled probability",
    value = prediction$outputs$allocation[, st_austell]
  )
) |>
  mutate(source = factor(source, unique(source)))

# Join to the small-area polygons, and locate the practice
mapped <- cornwall_lsoa |>
  select(lsoa) |>
  inner_join(shares, by = "lsoa")
site <- filter(cornwall_gp, practice == st_austell)
xy <- st_coordinates(site)

ggplot(mapped) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = value, colour = value), linewidth = 0.1) +
  geom_sf(data = site, shape = 21, fill = "white", size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~source) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    name = "Share of\nregistered\nresidents",
    limits = c(0, 1),
    aesthetics = c("fill", "colour")
  ) +
  # A 50 x 40 km window around the practice
  coord_sf(xlim = xy[1] + c(-25000, 25000), ylim = xy[2] + c(-20000, 20000)) +
  labs(title = "Registration with St Austell Health Group (white point)") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(margin = margin(b = 8)))
```

![Two maps of small areas around St Austell: the observed share of
residents registered with St Austell Health Group and the modelled
probability; the modelled catchment is centred on the same place but
spreads more widely.](reference/figures/README-clm-map-1.png)

The model reproduces the catchment’s location but spreads it more widely
than the observed registrations. Registrations record where residents
are registered, not how often they visit. The population grid (WorldPop
2020) and the registrations (NHS England, 2026) are different sources
and dates. Data sources and licences are listed in
`system.file("COPYRIGHTS", package = "spax")`.

## Continue the allocation workflow

| Function | Purpose |
|:---|:---|
| [`prepare_allocation()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/prepare_allocation.md) | Align IDs, validate inputs, record units and support, and prepare compact numeric inputs. |
| [`clm_allocation()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/clm_allocation.md) | Declare corrected static CLM with Gaussian, exponential or power travel decay, or a kernel declared with [`decay_kernel()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/decay_kernel.md). |
| [`fit_allocation()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/fit_allocation.md) | Fit a selected output from explicit starts and retain diagnostics. |
| [`evaluate_allocation()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/evaluate_allocation.md) | Evaluate supplied parameters, including a newly prepared supply scenario. |
| [`predict_allocation()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/predict_allocation.md) | Predict requested origins against saved facility loads; maps are explicit. |
| [`bootstrap_allocation()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/bootstrap_allocation.md) | Run the separately supported conditional facility-case bootstrap. |

[`vignette("model-choice", package = "spax")`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/articles/model-choice.md)
compares an FCA index and the static CLM on the same Cornwall inputs and
explains what each output means.

A supply scenario requires preparing the changed system and evaluating
it at the selected parameters. Supply can change attraction, allocation
and loads. This is a model-based comparison, not a causal intervention
estimate.

The bootstrap has a narrower scope than fitting: static CLM with a
fitted outside mass `v0` and a decay kernel that is smooth in `sigma`
(built in, or declared with
[`decay_kernel()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/decay_kernel.md);
a fitted `beta` is allowed), complete whole facility counts and an
unweighted Poisson original fit. It requires an explicit event,
reference period and independent-facility sampling declaration. The
Cornwall fit above targets small area × practice flows, so it is outside
this method.
[`vignette("facility-bootstrap", package = "spax")`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/articles/facility-bootstrap.md)
supplies a generated example with all 399 attempts and a paired supply
comparison;
[`vignette("allocation-workflow", package = "spax")`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/articles/allocation-workflow.md)
covers fitting, prediction, a supply scenario and fresh-session export
on the Cornwall data.

Conditional percentile intervals require an eligible original, a
complete run of 399 attempts and at least 380 finite successful values
for the quantity. Failed attempts and successful inner-boundary fits
remain visible. Coverage was evaluated for Gaussian decay with fitted
`sigma` and `v0`, in generated 80-origin/40-facility designs under
tested fixed-input laws; other kernels and a fitted `beta` use the same
procedure without a separate coverage study. This is not a universal
coverage guarantee or evidence for an application’s observation law. No
spatial simultaneous intervals are provided.

## IDs, support and saved results

Keep facility IDs on supply, travel and observations; named axes align
independently. Unnamed inputs are positional. Distinguish known zero
demand, unknown demand and excluded origins. Only included positive
demand contributes to fitted facility loads. For CLM prediction, unknown
travel and known absence (`Inf`) have different meanings; inspect
validity flags rather than replacing all missing values with zero.
Declare compatible units and reference periods; the interface does not
convert them.

Use [`coef()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/coef.html),
[`fitted()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/fitted.values.html),
[`summary()`](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/summary.html),
[`plot()`](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/plot.html) and
[`as.data.frame()`](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/as.data.frame.html)
to inspect saved allocation results. CSV drops R attributes, so keep an
RDS bundle with declarations and support metadata. See
[`help("allocation-compatibility", package = "spax")`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/spax-package.md)
before reusing older private fits: corrected CLM and legacy `huff_decay`
have different output meanings, and older objects may need regeneration
for current prediction/reporting.

## Contributing and license

Report reproducible issues or discuss larger changes on the [project
repository](https://github.com/Songyosr/spax). Package code uses the MIT
license; see [LICENSE](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/LICENSE.md). The
bundled Cornwall GP example data are openly licensed third-party
material (Open Government Licence v3.0 and Creative Commons
Attribution), which the MIT license does not cover. The installed notice
file, `system.file("COPYRIGHTS", package = "spax")` (source
`inst/COPYRIGHTS`), lists each source and its required attribution; the
exact Creative Commons version of the travel-friction source is still
unconfirmed.

# Package index

## Package Overview and Compatibility

Choose a workflow, preserve input meaning and reuse saved results safely

- [`spax`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/spax-package.md)
  [`spax-package`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/spax-package.md)
  [`allocation-compatibility`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/spax-package.md)
  : Spatial accessibility and allocation modeling

## Public FCA Accessibility

Raster accessibility surfaces with model-specific normalization and
independent supply indicators

- [`spax_2sfca()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/spax_2sfca.md)
  : Calculate Original Two-Step Floating Catchment Area (2SFCA)
  accessibility scores
- [`spax_e2sfca()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/spax_e2sfca.md)
  : Calculate Enhanced Two-Step Floating Catchment Area (E2SFCA)
  accessibility scores
- [`spax_m2sfca()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/spax_m2sfca.md)
  : Calculate Modified Two-Step Floating Catchment Area (M2SFCA)
  accessibility scores
- [`spax_3sfca()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/spax_3sfca.md)
  : Calculate Three-Step Floating Catchment Area (3SFCA) accessibility
  scores
- [`spax_huff2sfca()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/spax_huff2sfca.md)
  : Calculate Huff-model Two-Step Floating Catchment Area (Huff-2SFCA)
  scores
- [`compute_access()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/compute_access.md)
  : Calculate spatial accessibility using weighted surfaces

## Experimental Allocation Workflow

One static CLM system: checked inputs, fitting, saved-load prediction,
supply scenarios and restricted conditional bootstrap

- [`prepare_allocation()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/prepare_allocation.md)
  : Prepare checked numeric inputs for an experimental allocation
  workflow
- [`clm_allocation()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/clm_allocation.md)
  : Declare corrected static CLM over checked allocation inputs
- [`fit_allocation()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/fit_allocation.md)
  : Calibrate a declared allocation model from explicit starting points
- [`evaluate_allocation()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/evaluate_allocation.md)
  : Evaluate a declared allocation model at supplied fixed parameters
- [`predict_allocation()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/predict_allocation.md)
  : Predict requested origins against a saved fitted or evaluated CLM
- [`bootstrap_allocation()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/bootstrap_allocation.md)
  : Conditional facility-case bootstrap for a fitted allocation
- [`check_allocation()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/check_allocation.md)
  [`print(`*`<ae_allocation_check>`*`)`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/check_allocation.md)
  [`as.data.frame(`*`<ae_allocation_check>`*`)`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/check_allocation.md)
  : Check what fitted facility counts identify in an allocation model
- [`compare_allocations()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/compare_allocations.md)
  [`print(`*`<ae_allocation_comparison>`*`)`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/compare_allocations.md)
  [`as.data.frame(`*`<ae_allocation_comparison>`*`)`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/compare_allocations.md)
  : Compare fitted allocations across model and input specifications
- [`coef(`*`<ae_problem_nfxp_fit>`*`)`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/allocation-fit-methods.md)
  [`coef(`*`<ae_multistart_fit>`*`)`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/allocation-fit-methods.md)
  [`fitted(`*`<ae_problem_nfxp_fit>`*`)`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/allocation-fit-methods.md)
  [`fitted(`*`<ae_multistart_fit>`*`)`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/allocation-fit-methods.md)
  [`summary(`*`<ae_multistart_fit>`*`)`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/allocation-fit-methods.md)
  : Inspect saved allocation fits without recomputation
- [`as.data.frame(`*`<ae_problem_nfxp_fit>`*`)`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/allocation-result-tables.md)
  [`as.data.frame(`*`<ae_multistart_fit>`*`)`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/allocation-result-tables.md)
  [`as.data.frame(`*`<ae_coverage>`*`)`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/allocation-result-tables.md)
  [`as.data.frame(`*`<ae_allocation_bootstrap>`*`)`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/allocation-result-tables.md)
  : Inspect saved allocation result tables
- [`print(`*`<ae_allocation_bootstrap>`*`)`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/allocation-bootstrap-methods.md)
  [`summary(`*`<ae_allocation_bootstrap>`*`)`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/allocation-bootstrap-methods.md)
  [`print(`*`<summary.ae_allocation_bootstrap>`*`)`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/allocation-bootstrap-methods.md)
  [`plot(`*`<ae_allocation_bootstrap>`*`)`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/allocation-bootstrap-methods.md)
  : Inspect a saved facility bootstrap
- [`print(`*`<summary.ae_multistart_fit>`*`)`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/print.summary.ae_multistart_fit.md)
  : Print a saved allocation multistart summary
- [`plot(`*`<ae_multistart_fit>`*`)`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/plot.ae_multistart_fit.md)
  : Plot saved diagnostics from the selected allocation fit

## Distance & Decay Functions

Functions for handling distance relationships

- [`calc_decay()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/calc_decay.md)
  : Calculate Spatial Distance Decay Weights
- [`decay_kernel()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/decay_kernel.md)
  [`print(`*`<spax_decay_kernel>`*`)`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/decay_kernel.md)
  : Declare a distance decay kernel
- [`calc_choice()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/calc_choice.md)
  : Compute Spatial Choice Probabilities
- [`calc_normalize()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/calc_normalize.md)
  : Normalize Spatial Weights
- [`calc_travel_time()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/calc_travel_time.md)
  : Travel times to facilities over a friction surface
- [`calc_demand()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/calc_demand.md)
  : Demand from population groups and group-specific rates

## Data Processing Functions

Functions for processing spatial data

- [`spread_weighted()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/spread_weighted.md)
  : Distribute values across weighted surfaces
- [`spread_access()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/spread_access.md)
  : Calculate spatial accessibility scores
- [`gather_weighted()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/gather_weighted.md)
  : Aggregate weighted values from a raster
- [`gather_demand()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/gather_demand.md)
  : Calculate demand captured by each service site
- [`rasterize_demand()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/rasterize_demand.md)
  : Convenience wrapper for Bayesian spatial updating
- [`transform_pmf()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/transform_pmf.md)
  : Transform input into a probability mass function (PMF)
- [`transform_demand()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/transform_demand.md)
  : Transform Case Count Data into Spatial Distribution

## Simulation & Sampling

Spatial probability and demand sampling helpers; distinct from
allocation bootstrap intervals

- [`sample_pmf()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/sample_pmf.md)
  : Sample Points from Probability Surface with Multiple Realizations
- [`update_pmf()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/update_pmf.md)
  : Update Probability Mass Function with Likelihood Surface
- [`transform_likelihood()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/transform_likelihood.md)
  : Transform Input to Likelihood Surface

Helper functions and data access

- [`read_spax()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/read_spax.md)
  : Read a spax object from disk
- [`save_spax()`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/save_spax.md)
  : Save a spax accessibility analysis

## Cornwall GP Example Data

Open data for NHS Cornwall and Isles of Scilly GP practices; see
inst/COPYRIGHTS for sources and licences

- [`cornwall_gp`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/cornwall_gp.md)
  : GP practices in Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly
- [`cornwall_lsoa`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/cornwall_lsoa.md)
  : Small areas of Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly
- [`cornwall_flows`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/cornwall_flows.md)
  : Registered patients by small area and practice
- [`cornwall_travel`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/cornwall_travel.md)
  : Travel time from each small area to each practice
- [`cornwall_pop`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/cornwall_pop.md)
  : Population grid for Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly
- [`cornwall_gp_travel`](https://songyosr.github.io/spax/reference/cornwall_gp_travel.md)
  : Travel-time grid to each Cornwall GP practice
